text:
julia: Trying to walk a new engineer through the Python Quickstart Docker Compose sample and it's failing on their Windows machine with 401s. anyone seen this?

mike: yup, we've had a few reports. usually env var mismatch or path mount weirdness. what does your docker-compose.yml look like?

julia: here's the snippet from the quickstart page:```yaml
version: '3'
services:
  app:
    build: .
    environment:
      - API_KEY=${API_KEY}
    volumes:
      - .:/app
    command: python example/app.py
``` the python snippet uses `Client(os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))` so the env var names don't line up. docs probably got updated in one place and not the other.

sam: oof. that mismatch would give a 401 because the client sees None and we send an unsigned request.

mike: also on Windows mounting `.:/app` with WSL vs Docker Desktop can make line endings or path permission differences. if their container runs as root but files created as a different uid, the example creds file in the repo might not be readable.

julia: @mike good call — the user said they were on Docker Desktop for Windows with shared drives enabled. they also mentioned the compose file in the repo uses `API_KEY` but the app expects `REDWOOD_API_KEY`.

hana: tagging the docs bot in case the quickstart has multiple places with the wrong var name. docs-bot: can you check `docs/quickstart/python/docker-compose` and the sample app?

docs-bot: Checked 3 files: docs/quickstart/python/docker-compose.md, examples/python/docker-compose/app.py, examples/python/.env.example. Found inconsistent env var usage: `.env.example` and `docker-compose.yml` use `API_KEY`, docs guide and app.py expect `REDWOOD_API_KEY`. Suggested fix: standardize on `REDWOOD_API_KEY`.

sam: we should also add a Windows troubleshooting note about path mounts and recommend `volume: - ./app:/app` (explicit dir) and `:cached` flags where appropriate.

julia: quick reproduction steps from the user: 1) clone repo 2) cp .env.example .env 3) set API_KEY=value 4) docker-compose up 5) app logs show `401 Unauthorized`

mike: quick local repro I did: I set both API_KEY and REDWOOD_API_KEY in .env, container used API_KEY so app still 401. changing docker-compose to `- REDWOOD_API_KEY=${REDWOOD_API_KEY}` fixes it.

hana: file link in the docs currently points to https://redwood.inference/docs/quickstart/python/docker-compose which 404s for me. seems like the docs permalink changed last week. could be two separate problems: broken link and var mismatch.

julia: I'm going to open a tiny PR to: 1) fix docker-compose.yml to use REDWOOD_API_KEY 2) update .env.example to show REDWOOD_API_KEY 3) add a short troubleshooting note for Windows volume mounts and file perms. will add a test that runs the sample app in CI with the env var set.

mike: thanks — please also add an inline comment in app.py so readers know what env var name to expect, and mention `REDWOOD_API_KEY` in the quickstart text.

julia: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/432 — includes changes and a short section: "Troubleshooting Docker Desktop on Windows". I linked the user who reported it.

sam: quick nit: the Python snippet on the docs page shows `from redwood import Client` but the package on PyPI is `redwood-inference`. Not sure if that was intentional (we alias) or a copy/paste mistake. worth checking so imports are consistent.

docs-bot: Noted. Search across docs repo: found 2 other pages importing `from redwood import Client`. Recommend searching the code samples and aligning to the packaged import.

julia: ok I'll add a follow-up PR to standardize the import examples (or add an explanatory note if we want to teach `from redwood import Client` is allowed).

hana: for the broken permalink I'll file an issue in the docs repo to re-add a redirect from the old path -> new path, so external links don't 404.

mike: also add a tiny integration test: `docker-compose run --rm app python -c "from redwood import Client; print('ok')"` to catch import/name drift. CI can run it in a linux container so we at least catch mismatched sample code before merge.

julia: PR merged to main for the var fix and Windows note. follow-up PR for imports created as #433.

sam: thanks everyone. lesson: small copy edits across docs + samples break onboarding pretty quickly.

julia: filing a short retro note to track these quickstart drift issues and maybe add a docs QA checklist for sample parity. :memo: :rocket:
